summary:
The Airport and Airway Extension Act of 2024 extends, principally through May 10 or May 11, 2024, Federal Aviation Administration program authorizations, Airport and Airway Trust Fund expenditure authority, aviation excise taxes, and related expiring aviation and counter-UAS authorities.

Title I amends title 49, United States Code, and related aviation statutes to continue FAA programs. Section 101 amends 49 U.S.C. § 48103(a) to authorize $2,041,120,218 for the Airport Improvement Program for the period October 1, 2023, through May 10, 2024. Amounts made available pursuant to that authorization may be obligated through September 30, 2024, subject to limitations specified in advance in appropriations Acts, and remain available until expended. For 49 U.S.C. §§ 47114, 47115, 47116, and 47117, the FAA Administrator must calculate apportionments as if the fiscal year 2024 amount were $3.35 billion and then reduce specified apportionments and § 47117(b), (f)(2) amounts by 39 percent. Section 101 also extends project grant authority under 49 U.S.C. § 47104(c) and the special apportionment rule in § 47114(c)(1)(J) to May 10, 2024.

Section 102 extends multiple expiring authorities, generally from March 8 or 9, 2024, to May 10 or 11, 2024, including aviation insurance authority under 49 U.S.C. § 44310(b), unmanned aircraft test ranges and special UAS authorities under 49 U.S.C. §§ 44803(h), 44807(d), and 44810(h), airport grant-related provisions under 49 U.S.C. §§ 47107(r)(3), 47115(i), 47141(f), and 47143(c), the commercial spaceflight “learning period” in 51 U.S.C. § 50905(c)(9), and specified provisions of prior FAA reauthorization Acts. It also authorizes $340,321,762 in supplemental discretionary funds under 49 U.S.C. § 47115(j)(4)(A) and $23,762,295 for weather reporting programs under 49 U.S.C. § 48105 for the October 1, 2023–May 10, 2024 period. Sections 103–105 authorize, respectively, $7,259,685,792 for FAA operations under 49 U.S.C. § 106(k), $1,794,357,923 for air navigation facilities and equipment under § 48101(a), and $155,368,852 for research, engineering, and development under § 48102(a), each for the same period. Section 106 increases and extends authorizations for Essential Air Service under 49 U.S.C. § 41742(a)(2) and small community air service development under § 41743(e)(2).

Title II amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. Section 201 extends Airport and Airway Trust Fund expenditure authority under 26 U.S.C. § 9502(d)(1) and the conforming transfer limitation in § 9502(e)(2) to May 11, 2024, and adds this Act to covered authorization Acts. Section 202 extends aviation fuel, ticket, cargo, and fractional ownership program tax provisions in 26 U.S.C. §§ 4081(d)(2)(B), 4261(k), 4271(d), 4043(d), 4083(b), and 4261(j) to May 10 or May 11, 2024, as specified. Title III, § 301 extends counter-UAS authorities under § 210G(i) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002, 6 U.S.C. § 124n(i), to May 11, 2024.
